title: SOME/IP: Add Filter String Support for Services and Methods
description:
## Summary

This change extends the SOME/IP dissector with optional filter strings for Services and Methods/Events. Users can now define custom filters like `someip.service.my_service` or `someip.method.my_method` to filter for specific services or methods more easily.

The implementation adds a new optional "Filter String" column to both the **Services UAT** and the **Methods UAT**. When these columns are left empty, the behavior remains exactly as before. Only when a filter string is specified, new dedicated filter fields (`someip.service.*` and `someip.method.*`) are dynamically created.

**This is a fully backward-compatible enhancement** - existing configurations and workflows continue to work without any modifications. The filter string feature is entirely optional.

## Motivation

Previously, SOME/IP Services and Methods could be filtered either by:
1. **Numeric IDs** (e.g., `someip.serviceid == 0x1234`) - cumbersome and hard to remember
2. **Generic string fields** (e.g., `someip.servicename == "DiagService"`) - error-prone due to case sensitivity and typos, with no autocomplete support

Both approaches had significant drawbacks, especially in complex network analysis scenarios. This enhancement introduces dedicated filter fields with proper autocomplete support, making filtering more robust and user-friendly. Users can now define meaningful text-based filters like `someip.service.diag` that appear in Wireshark's autocomplete dropdown and are not case-sensitive.

### Filtering in Wireshark

**Old approach (still works but has limitations):**
```
someip.serviceid == 0x1234                    # Numeric - hard to remember
someip.servicename == "DiagService"           # String matching - case sensitive, no autocomplete, typo-prone
someip.methodname == "ReadData"               # String matching - same issues
```

**New approach (recommended):**
```
someip.service.diag              # All packets for DiagService - autocomplete supported!
someip.method.diag_read          # Only ReadData calls - autocomplete supported!
someip.service.media             # All packets for MediaService
someip.method.media_play         # Only PlayPause calls
```

**Benefits:**
- ✅ Autocomplete in Wireshark's filter bar for both services AND methods
- ✅ No case sensitivity issues
- ✅ Type-safe (filter won't work if service/method is not configured)
- ✅ Clear and concise syntax
- ✅ Optional - only active when filter string column is filled in the UAT

### Backward Compatibility

- **New optional UAT columns**: A "Filter String" column is added to both Services and Methods UATs
- **If left empty**: Behavior is identical to previous versions - no new filter fields are created
- **If filled**: Dynamic filter fields `someip.service.*` and `someip.method.*` are automatically registered
- Existing configurations continue to work without changes
- **All existing filter methods remain functional:**
  - Numeric filters: `someip.serviceid == 0x1234`, `someip.methodid == 0x0001`
  - String filters: `someip.servicename == "DiagService"`, `someip.methodname == "ReadData"`
  - New filter fields: `someip.service.diag`, `someip.method.diag_read` (when configured)
- The new filter fields provide autocomplete and are less error-prone than string matching

notes.body: You are right. I am sorry.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22358/diffs?diff_id=1571446584&start_sha=1fc1e209eddf3ed4c419efdeca2e7822f0b4d16e#939d770822ae6ea95241591ea801aa75281c2840_54_54)

So what was the reason for creating all of the UATs for SOME/IP in the first place?  Is it because SOME/IP has a lot of user defined/application specific enumerations and each "application" has its own list of services/methods, so different groups/companies each have their own set of preferences for SOME/IP that describe their application layer?  Are there no "standard" services/methods that would be part of (large) switch statements for dissection?
My objection to this patch (and some of the SOME/IP functionality) is that Wireshark does have mechanisms already in place for these features, but they are being recreated "manually" which could result in inconsistent behavior between SOME/IP and other protocols. I don't like to see "exceptions" added for individual protocol behavior that should be more global for any/all dissectors.  This functionality just seems to be what value_strings are within dissection code.  And if there are dynamically registered fields, they should be able to be accompanied by dynamically created value_strings.

Yes, SOME/IP offers the ability to dissect the payload serialized with the SOME/IP serializer. This part is highly customizable. Configuring SOME/IP using UATs is the current state of affairs. To avoid breaking changes, I have only implemented compatible extensions.
